Reading the ratings

V2 and V1 each lost twice to Random. Both lost one game on the same forced opening. Random started with three 7s against three 3s and cleared its last number on tap five. Play the forced line.

Rules, policies and estimation

Each player receives a uniformly drawn sorted triple of digits 1–9. A fair draw decides the first seat. The bots swap sides on the same opening, with a new policy seed. A win requires clearing every number or leaving the opponent without a legal tap. The timeout is 10,000 two-tap rounds without a withdrawal. The referee replays every tap and checks the full board history.

V2 uses its released 500,000-node, depth-18 settings. V1 uses 4,500 nodes and depth 8. Heuristic prioritizes an immediate win, then avoids allowing an immediate opponent win or withdrawal and prefers withdrawing its own number. Random samples uniformly from the legal value-pairs.

The Bradley–Terry model estimates a single rating for each bot using the 400-point Elo scale. Random is fixed at zero. The 95% percentile intervals use 2,000 resamples of 1,000 opening draws. Each draw retains its two seat assignments and all six pairings.
